races.title: State Assembly, District 78
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Chris Ward
cands.bio: Democrat and incumbent California Assemblymember for District 78 (San Diego) since December 2020. Served on the San Diego City Council, District 3, 2016–2020. Earlier worked as an environmental planner, a cancer researcher at UC San Diego, and chief of staff to State Senator Marty Block.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed on Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.
San Diego County Democratic Party endorsed him in 2024.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ward was raised or when he moved to California. We found no record of his positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, school choice, or police pay and pensions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. The sources describe a 2022 bill to prioritize dense urban development while limiting sprawl, but not its details or his role, so we did not score it. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: San Diego City Council member 2016–2020 (chaired its Economic Development and Intergovernmental Relations Committee); state Assemblymember since 2020; chief of staff to State Senator Marty Block; environmental planner at EDAW; master's in public policy and urban planning from Harvard.
qual.why: Prior legislative service at the city and state level, plus policy and land-use planning work and legislative staff experience, puts him in the high band. Committee seats were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: Was involved in gun violence reduction legislation signed into law in 2022 that enables lawsuits against gun manufacturers and retailers for negligence.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site says "California's housing crisis can only be solved with one thing: housing," and says he will work to cut red tape to build more middle-income homes while maintaining neighborhood quality of life.

cands.name: Payton Galvez
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 78 in 2026. Lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Christopher Ward. The sources reviewed give no occupation or prior offices.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements and voter guide recommendations: Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Conservative California, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Payton Galvez was born or raised, when they came to California, or their occupation and work history. Galvez has held no elected office that we could document. Galvez did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no other statements of position on data centers, development, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or other issues. We found no documented actions, controversies, or foreign ties.
